newsitem.title: USA: Scattered rain aids some Iowa crops, not others.
newsitem.headline: Scattered rain aids some Iowa crops, not others.

text.p: Scattered showers during the week ended Sunday aided Iowa corn and soybeans that received the moisture, but crops that were missed were stressed by dry conditions, according to the state's weekly Agricultural Statistics Service report.
Temperatures finally rose to above normal levels late in the week, which stressed soybean fields that were missed by the rain.

Corn stands were 93 percent of normal. The crop was rated 15 percent excellent, 58 good, 23 fair and four poor. The average height was 12 inches, which could not be compared with a year ago. On June 21, 1996, corn was 18 inches tall.

Soybean emergence was ahead of normal but development was slow. Dry conditions slowed development of late-planted and replanted fields. Four percent of the acreage had to be replanted or will be replanted.

Oats improved slightly with the crop rated 58 percent good to excellent, 35 percent fair, six poor and one very poor. Seventeen percent of the crop was headed, versus six a year ago and the 32 average.
Winter wheat was 60 percent headed. The crop was rated 13 percent condition excellent, 61 good, 19 fair, five poor and two very poor.
